title: What is Type Inference?
overview: Type inference is a TypeScript feature where the compiler automatically determines the type of a variable based on its assigned value.

example.title: Inference Example

title: Implicit Type Inference
overview: When a variable is initialized with a value, TypeScript automatically assigns the appropriate type without requiring manual type declaration.

example.title: Implicit Type

title: Inference in Functions
overview: TypeScript can infer function return types based on the returned value. This reduces unnecessary type writing.

example.title: Function Inference

title: When to Add Explicit Types
overview: Although TypeScript can infer many types, developers should add explicit types when working with function parameters, complex objects, or shared code.

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned how TypeScript automatically detects types, where inference works, and when developers should manually define types.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ TypeScript can detect types automatically.
✔ Inference reduces unnecessary code.
